title: Personal Checking: Restriction and Charge-Off of Persistently Overdrawn Accounts
content:
## Starting point

Every Personal Checking negative episode is timed from the date the ledger balance first went below zero, as held on the account record.

## Restriction

An active account is restricted once the tier's restriction period, in calendar days, has passed since that date. Counting starts with the day after the balance went negative as day 1; restriction falls due from the date that lies the restriction period after that negative date, the boundary day itself included, and on every later date.

During restriction the bank pays nothing that would leave or put the balance under zero — such debits are returned or declined — and no overdraft fees build up. A restricted account goes back to active as soon as a day ends with its ledger balance at zero or above.

## Charge-off

A restricted account is charged off once the tier's charge-off period, in calendar days, has passed since the same date, counted the same way: day 1 is the following day, and charge-off is due on or after that date plus the charge-off period.

The charge-off books one write-off credit equal to the size of the negative balance, which brings the ledger to zero; the deficit is then handled by recovery outside the Personal Checking terms. A charged-off account is afterwards closed administratively. Offers by a customer to pay a charged-off deficit are not covered by this rule.

## Timeline (hypothetical restriction period of 20 days and charge-off period of 40 days)

| Balance negative since | Date | Status reached |
|---|---|---|
| 1 July 2026 | 20 July 2026 (day 19) | still active |
| 1 July 2026 | 21 July 2026 (day 20) | restriction due |
| 1 July 2026 | 9 August 2026 (day 39) | restricted, charge-off not yet due |
| 1 July 2026 | 10 August 2026 (day 40) | charge-off due |

## Q&A

**If a deposit restores the balance to zero during the restriction, what happens?** The account returns to active at the end of that day and the date the balance went negative is cleared.

**Are overdraft fees charged on items presented while restricted?** No; such debits are returned or declined without overdraft fees.
